GHz third harmonic superconducting cavities have been used to increase the peak bunch current and to mitigate non-linear distortions in the longitudinal phase space caused by the 1.3 GHz sinusoidal drive voltage of the accelerator (1). The power coupler, a critical component for efficient energy transfer between the RF source and the high-power cavities, often represents a significant bottleneck in performance due to impedance mismatches and heat load limitations. In this study, we present comprehensive computer simulations employing finite element methods to model a novel distributed-lump-element power coupler optimized for the unique AC transmission line characteristics of 3.9 GHz third harmonic cavities. The simulation results are compared against experimental data from prototype devices to validate the design. Optimization techniques, incorporating iterative parameter sweeps and constraint-based methods to minimize reflected power and maximize coupling efficiency, are applied to identify an enhanced coupler configuration. The optimized coupler design demonstrates up to 2.1% improvement in coupling efficiency and a 30% reduction in RF losses at 3.9 GHz, with robust thermal stability under high-power operation. These findings pave the way for improved acceleration performance in Fermilab’s superconducting linac and future facilities employing high-frequency RF systems.
